newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japanese toy takes Manila by storm, alarms schools.
newsitem.headline: Japanese toy takes Manila by storm, alarms schools.

text.p: Even the Philippine education secretary found the tamagotchi so addictive he decided it should be kept out of the hands of the country's school children.
On Thursday, Ricardo Gloria signed a memorandum ordering schools to discourage children from bringing the Japanese virtual pet toy to class.
"He bought one to see for himself and, after four hours with it, he told us, 'With this, school children won't pay attention to their teachers any more'," an education spokeswoman said.
Tamagotchi - "loveable egg" in Japanese - has become so popular in private schools that children spend more time with it than listening to their teachers, she said.
Shaped like an egg, the toy has a computer-like screen showing the image of a pet that has to be fed, bathed, taken for a walk and put to sleep. It can die of neglect.
"It awakens in the child an early sense of death, which is not good," the spokeswoman said.
Instead of tamagotchi - already banned in schools in Taiwan and Hong Kong - teachers should advise children to take care of real pets, "like dogs and rabbits", Gloria said.
